papers.title: From sequence space to ecological function: microbiome-derived antimicrobial peptides as community effectors and therapeutic leads.
papers.summary: Review of microbiome-derived antimicrobial peptides: bacteriocins, RiPPs, cryptic short-ORF peptides, and embedded antimicrobial regions. Genome mining, metagenomics, and machine learning have massively expanded candidate catalogues, but native expression, producer assignment, ecological function, and in vivo relevance remain unproven for most predicted molecules. The authors frame these peptides as both therapeutic leads and ecological effectors mediating microbial competition and colonisation resistance.

papers.title: Mesolens imaging in microbiology.
papers.summary: Review of the Mesolens, a microscope objective combining low magnification with high numerical aperture to deliver sub-micron resolution across multi-millimetre fields of view and millimetre-deep specimens. Applications include visualising biofilm nutrient transport channels in E. coli and cross-kingdom Candida albicans-Staphylococcus aureus biofilms. Covers widefield, confocal, light-sheet, TIRF, and standing-wave mesoscopy variants, plus specimen preparation and computational acquisition workflows.

papers.title: The roles of symmetric and asymmetric parental histone recycling in cell fate, development, and disease.
papers.summary: Review of parental histone recycling during DNA replication, where replisome histone chaperones distribute parental histones to leading and lagging strands to preserve epigenetic memory. Recycling is usually symmetric, but asymmetric recycling occurs naturally in asymmetrically dividing cells or via replisome manipulation. Asymmetric inheritance generates distinct epigenetic states at a locus, driving differential gene expression and divergent cell fates in developing multicellular organisms, with implications for disease.

papers.title: SF3B4 "reads" RNA that is methylated by METTL16.
papers.summary: Using an RNA-binding protein domain array screen, pull-down assays, and RIP-seq with RIP-qPCR validation, the authors identify the spliceosomal protein SF3B4 as a previously unrecognized m6A reader. SF3B4 preferentially associates with the GRAGRA motif, matching RNAs methylated by METTL16 rather than the METTL3/14 complex. Shared SF3B4/METTL16 targets include the BCR and MET oncogene transcripts, linking SF3B4 to RNA metabolism downstream of METTL16-mediated methylation.

papers.title: Atypical p38 kinase signaling and pathological impact on human health.
papers.summary: Review of atypical p38 MAPK activation, where p38alpha autophosphorylates through direct protein-protein interactions rather than upstream MKK3/MKK6 kinases. Known activators include TAK1-binding protein 1, ZAP-70, hepatitis C virus core protein, and Toxoplasma gondii GRA24. The authors compare structural determinants and substrate engagement against canonical signaling, and link atypical activation to cardiac ischemia, infection, inflammation, and vascular dysfunction, establishing it as a distinct regulatory paradigm.

papers.title: High-resolution profiling of bacterial transcriptomes by SEnd-seq.
papers.summary: Review of SEnd-seq, a high-throughput method capturing both 5' and 3' RNA ends simultaneously to reconstruct full-length bacterial transcripts at single-nucleotide resolution. Applied across species including E. coli and Mycobacterium tuberculosis, it detects low-abundance RNAs and supports genetic, chemical, and functional perturbations. The technique reveals transcription start and termination sites, RNA processing events, and coordinately regulated transcripts, informing antibiotic target discovery.

papers.title: Conserved structural elements in Gα subunit switch regions are necessary for efficient inactivation by RGS proteins.
papers.summary: Computational energy calculations across Galpha-RGS complexes identify conserved residues in switch I and II regions as central to RGS-mediated GTPase-activating protein activity. Switch I interactions rely on backbone electrostatics, while switch II depends on side-chain electrostatics; mutagenesis confirms individual switch I side chains are dispensable, but disrupting the interface abolishes GAP activity. Switch II alanine substitutions severely reduce activity. Results enable engineered Galpha proteins and RGS-binding inhibitors.

papers.title: Lipid moieties of sonic hedgehog contribute to but are not essential for interaction with its inhibitor, WIF1.
papers.summary: Surface plasmon resonance and reporter assays compare human WIF1 binding to lipidated versus non-lipidated sonic hedgehog (SHH). WIF1, originally characterized as a Wnt antagonist, also inhibits SHH signaling. Lipidated SHH shows modestly but significantly higher WIF1 affinity than unmodified SHH, indicating the lipid moieties contribute to but are not essential for the interaction. This parallels Wnt, where lipid modifications similarly mediate morphogen-receptor recognition.

papers.title: The role of CYP3A-CYP2E1 interactions in activation of CYP3A enzymes by chronic alcohol exposure.
papers.summary: In liver microsomes from 23 donors with documented alcohol exposure, CYP3A activity increased with chronic alcohol consumption without corresponding enzyme level changes. Metabolism rates instead correlated with alcohol-inducible CYP2E1 content, which itself poorly metabolizes the CYP3A substrates used. Incorporating purified CYP2E1 into CYP3A4-containing membranes increased activity, and crosslinking mass spectrometry confirmed physical CYP2E1-CYP3A4 complexes. Results indicate direct protein interactions functionally activate CYP3A enzymes.

papers.title: Molecular dissection of the Cereibacter sphaeroides spheroidene monooxygenase.
papers.summary: Cereibacter sphaeroides spheroidene monooxygenase (CrtA) introduces a keto group into spheroidene during carotenoid biosynthesis. Using a CrtA mutant preserving downstream bchId expression, truncation mapping identified the minimal active enzyme and structural modelling revealed a histidine axial ligand to heme plus two threonines near the bound carotenoid. The proline-rich C-terminal extension mediates CrtA association with other membrane proteins into high-molecular-mass complexes, explaining residual photoheterotrophic growth phenotypes.

papers.title: Modified meiosis in the tardigrade Hypsibius exemplaris maintains heterozygosity across the genome.
papers.summary: The asexual tardigrade Hypsibius exemplaris undergoes incomplete meiosis I with no cell division, followed by a complete meiosis II-like division, maintaining genome-wide heterozygosity across generations. Combined cytology and genomics confirmed allele inheritance patterns, and heterozygous variants in transcriptionally active genes suggest divergence between alleles over time. This establishes the reproductive mechanism in H. exemplaris and adds to known asexual animals reproducing clonally despite long-term costs.

papers.title: Toward standardization in arthropod and biodiversity genome projects.
papers.summary: Surveying 100 arthropod genome papers from 2024, the authors review standards across seven project stages from budgeting to annotation. Long-read assembly is now standard with consistent contiguity and gene-content reporting, but pre- and post-assembly procedures, ethical collection compliance, sample vouchering, curation, and extended quality metrics vary widely. Annotation practices are especially inconsistent, with low submission of annotations to centralized databases. Recommendations target harmonized reporting for genome reusability.

papers.title: Should we build single-cell lineage trees from gene expression data?
papers.summary: Theoretical and empirical analysis of whether single-cell transcriptomic data can reconstruct lineage trees. Under a model of neutral gene expression, accurate reconstruction of even small trees requires thousands of independent neutral traits, a condition rarely met because non-neutral developmental signals dominate expression. Measurement sampling errors can destroy remaining lineage signal. Gene expression data thus have limited potential as natural lineage recorders without rigorous further validation for phylogenetic inference.

papers.title: Solving the mechanism of Notch activation: a geneticist's perspective.
papers.summary: Perspective essay continuing a geneticist's account of Notch signaling discoveries through the first quarter of the 21st century. Following the 20th-century identification of core components and the novel cleavage mechanism of signal transduction, the author illustrates how genetic approaches remained essential for framing and resolving mechanistic questions, even as Notch activation events are now elucidated in structural detail. Notch acts as oncogene or tumor suppressor depending on cellular context.

papers.title: Developmental patterning of adipose tissue by abd-A and Abd-B homeotic genes in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.summary: In Drosophila larval fat body, abdominal-A and Abdominal-B homeotic genes pattern segmental adipose tissue identity. The authors identify cis-regulatory elements driving abdomen-specific expression and use yeast one-hybrid screening to define a regulatory network: Lola, Lolal, and Combgap repress abd-B, while Piragua and Seven up activate it, forming feedback loops modulated by Wnt signaling. CUT&RUN confirms DTCF/Pangolin and Abd-B occupancy at target loci, explaining anterior-posterior adipocyte heterogeneity.

papers.title: De novo genes originate in regions of ancestrally closed chromatin.
papers.summary: ATAC-seq across Drosophila melanogaster genotypes shows open chromatin correlates with expression of young de novo genes in the male accessory gland, whereas homologous sequences in D. simulans and D. yakuba remain closed, indicating accessibility is a derived state. Mapping cis-regulatory variants across 29 genotypes links local sequence changes to transcription for at least five de novo genes. Most de novo genes thus arise through new regulatory sequences requiring multiple DNA changes rather than co-opting ancestral ones.

papers.title: Parallel transcriptome adaptation during recent evolution of the Drosophila testis.
papers.summary: First comparative continent-scale transcriptomic analysis of male reproductive tract, testis, and accessory gland in Drosophila melanogaster and D. simulans, including ancestral-range populations for both species. Both underwent recent global range expansions, D. melanogaster dispersing from sub-Saharan Africa roughly 13,000 years ago and D. simulans from Madagascar, providing a framework to test parallel transcriptome adaptation driven by migration and natural selection across recently colonized continents.

papers.title: Candida glabrata YPK2 is a multidrug susceptibility locus.
papers.summary: In Candida glabrata (Nakaseomyces glabratus), the UPC2A transcriptional regulator of azole susceptibility physically associates with the Ypk2 AGC kinase. Ypk2 deletion increases susceptibility to fluconazole, caspofungin, and other major antifungal classes, impairing induction of erg genes while leaving CDR1 transporter induction intact. RNA-seq shows each antifungal drug elicits a distinct transcriptional response differentially altered by YPK2 loss, establishing YPK2 as a multidrug susceptibility locus in this pathogenic yeast.

papers.title: Coexistence of piRNA and KZFP defense systems: evolutionary dynamics of layered defense against transposable elements.
papers.summary: Mathematical modelling of transposable element (TE) defense explores how piRNA and Kruppel-associated box zinc-finger protein (KZFP) systems coexist despite functional redundancy. Key asymmetry: piRNA suppression requires ongoing TE activity, whereas KZFPs silence constitutively. The model derives analytical conditions under which KZFPs invade an established TE-piRNA equilibrium, explaining how this recent innovation diversified in piRNA-occupied genomes and providing a theoretical framework for layered genome defense evolution.

papers.title: Creation and manipulation of bipartite expression transgenes in C. elegans using phiC31 recombinase.
papers.summary: Method paper introducing recombination-mediated homolog exchange in C. elegans: genetically encoded phiC31 recombinase converts driver-reporter transgene pairs from trans to cis configuration using attB- and attP-tagged lines. A companion microinjection approach, recombination-mediated integration, inserts whole driver or reporter plasmids into existing attP or attB landing sites. These tools simplify segregation of bipartite expression systems in genetic crosses and extend to creating and manipulating other transgenes.

papers.title: Functional landscape of zebrafish gonadotropins and receptors: a comprehensive genetic analysis.
papers.summary: Comprehensive genetic dissection of zebrafish gonadotropin signaling using single through quadruple mutants of fshb, lhb, fshr, and lhcgr. Zebrafish LH activates both Lhcgr and Fshr, creating a noncanonical LH-Fshr pathway alongside canonical Fsh-Fshr and Lh-Lhcgr routes. Double mutants confirm all three pathways function, transcriptomics reveal Lh mechanisms driving oocyte maturation via Fshr, triple mutants show ligand-independent receptor activity in spermatogenesis, and quadruple mutants are all-male with underdeveloped infertile gonads.

papers.title: Synergistic actions of Nup43 and Myosin VI drive actin cone assembly during Drosophila spermiogenesis.
papers.summary: In Drosophila, the nucleoporin Nup43 is essential for fertility: null mutants of both sexes are sterile. Female sterility reflects disrupted early embryonic mitoses; male sterility involves sperm development arrest at the canoe stage with impaired nuclear elongation, shaping, and actin cone assembly during individualization complex formation. Myosin VI (Jar) interacts with Nup43 and rescues actin cone assembly but not sterility. Nup43 thus facilitates sperm individualization through Jar-dependent actin cone assembly, a noncanonical pore-independent role.

papers.title: Identification of two Cryptococcus neoformans heme transporters involved in Fhb1-mediated nitrosative stress protection in a fission yeast model.
papers.summary: Cryptococcus neoformans flavohemoglobin Fhb1 protects against nitrosative stress but requires exogenous heme. Heterologous expression in fission yeast identified two uncharacterized C. neoformans transporters, CnStr1 and CnStr3, that enable Fhb1-mediated nitric oxide detoxification and rescue heme-dependent growth defects in heme-biosynthesis mutants. Coimmunoprecipitation confirms Fhb1-Str interactions, and C. neoformans strains lacking CnStr1/CnStr3 show heme-dependent growth defects and fail nitrosative stress protection without the hemophore Cig1.

papers.title: Recombinant ubbR promoter enables highly efficient tamoxifen-inducible Cre recombination in embryonic and adult zebrafish.
papers.summary: A recombinant zebrafish ubiquitin promoter (ubbR), combining the native ubiquitin promoter with a carp beta-actin2 intronic enhancer, outperforms both parent promoters at all embryonic stages tested. Integrated via phiC31-mediated targeted insertion, the ubbr:creERT2 driver line achieves high-level recombination of floxed alleles in adult zebrafish tissues, addressing the historical limitation of insufficient recombination for complete conditional gene inactivation. The promoter retains high activity at multiple genomic integration sites.

papers.title: Allele frequencies at recessive disease genes are mainly determined by pleiotropic effects in heterozygotes.
papers.summary: Comparing observed loss-of-function variant frequencies against mutation-selection balance predictions, the authors find nearly all human recessive disease genes show variant frequencies too low for purely recessive selection. UK Biobank quantitative trait analysis reveals widespread heterozygous effects on traits, indicating most selection on pathogenic mutations operates through heterozygote pleiotropy rather than homozygote disadvantage. Very few human genes therefore follow the classic recessive mutation-selection balance model.

papers.title: Large impact of genetic data processing steps on stability and reproducibility of set-based analyses in genome-wide association studies.
papers.summary: Set-based GWAS analyses, including rare-variant gene-based tests, polygenic score construction, and fine-mapping, are highly sensitive to seemingly minor data-processing pipeline choices rarely documented in publications. Through model misspecification framing, analytical calculations of power loss and bias, simulations, and a pancreatic cancer example where the top ATM association disappears under slightly different data preparation, the authors demonstrate reproducibility risks and provide tools to quantify and avoid these data-quality obstacles.

papers.title: Diverse microbial metal resistance and novel metal cycling organisms in copper/nickel mine tailings.
papers.summary: Integrated metagenomics and metaproteomics across vertical geochemical gradients in legacy copper/nickel mine tailings in Sudbury, Ontario recovered 454 metagenome-assembled genomes, including uncultured lineages Ca. Eremiobacterota and SZUA-79. Custom hidden Markov models identified widespread, diverse metal resistance genes whose abundances did not correlate with measured copper, nickel, or iron concentrations, suggesting broad encoding regardless of local metal levels. Proteomics confirmed in situ expression of selected resistance and iron/sulfur cycling genes.

papers.title: PPP1R3C functions as a tumor suppressor in endometrial cancer through promotion of glycogen synthesis.
papers.summary: PPP1R3C, a protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit that promotes glycogen synthesis and inhibits glycogen breakdown, is strongly downregulated in uterine corpus endometrial cancer tissues. Ectopic PPP1R3C expression causes cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in HEC1A and HEC1B endometrial cancer cells and inhibits xenograft tumour growth in BALB/c nude mice. Glycogen synthase inhibition abrogates this growth suppression, indicating PPP1R3C acts as a tumour suppressor in endometrial cancer through activating glycogen synthesis.

papers.title: Single-cell multimodal analysis reveals enhancer and transcription factor regulatory dynamics during human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte differentiation.
papers.summary: SHARE-seq profiling of human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte differentiation resolves sequential developmental states including iPSCs, mesodermal cells, progenitors, cardiomyocytes, and off-target populations. Peak-to-gene linkage identifies cell state-associated enhancer-gene relationships including the myh6/myh7 locus, while pseudotime analysis tracks progressive chromatin and transcriptional remodeling. In silico perturbation and gene regulatory network inference nominate transcription factors driving cardiac lineage progression, providing a multimodal resource for differentiation studies.

papers.title: Sperm as a multilayered epigenetic information system: encoding and transmission of paternal environmental signals.
papers.summary: Review of sperm as a multilayered epigenetic information system. During spermatogenesis and epididymal maturation, the paternal germline establishes DNA methylation, retained histones and modifications, chromatin-associated factors, and small RNAs, all environmentally responsive. Animal models show paternal diet, stress, toxicants, and inflammatory challenges alter these layers at development and metabolism loci. Evidence for transmission to offspring phenotypes exists but remains largely observational in humans, confounded by genetics and shared environment.

papers.title: Multifaceted roles of KCTD17 in cellular homeostasis and disease.
papers.summary: Review of KCTD17, a BTB/POZ-domain potassium channel tetramerization domain-containing protein functioning as an adaptor in Cullin 3-based E3 ubiquitin ligase complexes. Through selective protein ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, KCTD17 influences organelle dynamics, differentiation, signaling, metabolic regulation, stress responses, and tissue remodeling. Effects are highly context-dependent across cell types and pathological states, though full substrate specificity, regulatory mechanisms, and therapeutic potential remain unresolved.

papers.title: Alzheimer's disease through the lens of mesenchymal drift: the collapse of cellular identity.
papers.summary: Review applying the mesenchymal drift framework to Alzheimer's disease: a stochastic, lineage-independent loss of cellular identity marked by epigenetic noise and profibrotic gene activation. In AD brains, neural progenitors differentiate prematurely, mature neurons dedifferentiate, endothelial cells acquire vascular fibrosis features, and glia lose homeostatic functions. Direct mesenchymal drift signature enrichment is confirmed in astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, pericytes, and APP-mutant iPSC-derived neural progenitors. The authors caution that apparent novel cell populations may reflect lineage blurring.

papers.title: Effect of decay on detection of chronic wasting disease (CWD) in lymph nodes using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).
papers.summary: Chronic wasting disease surveillance typically requires fresh retropharyngeal lymph node or obex tissue for ELISA or immunohistochemistry. Testing lymph nodes from known CWD-positive white-tailed deer in Illinois decayed for up to 12 months at 4 and 27 degrees Celsius, ELISA detected prions in 100% of samples across all experimental groups, though detection percentages varied over time. This is the first demonstration that USDA-APHIS-approved ELISA works on extensively degraded lymph nodes, enabling surveillance on suboptimal tissue.
